subject: Re: Crypto handshake and KMS orchestration for on-prem VPC deployment
content:
From: Sasha Patel <ops@acme-corp.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn.shaw@bankcorp.com
Date: 2026-10-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: KMS/HSM plan for on-prem Private deployment (initial)

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the quick call this morning. As discussed, Acme is planning a pilot of Redwood Private in our NYC VPC (air-gapped subnet) and we need to validate the key custody and encryption handshake. Topline asks:

- We want BYOK for model keys and tenant KEKs with HSM-backed root keys.
- We need a network diagram showing required ports, egress rules, and an attestation step for vendor HSM initial import.
- Rotation cadence: quarterly for KEKs, annual for HSM root; confirm support for split-key escrow in the flow.

Can you share a concrete deployment sequence we can run against our infra team and the vendor? Also attach any sample runbook for incident key rollback.

Thanks,
Sasha Patel
Head of Cloud Ops, Acme Corp

--
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Sasha Patel <ops@acme-corp.com>
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-10T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: KMS/HSM plan for on-prem Private deployment (initial)

Sasha —

Appreciate the clear summary. I sketched a minimal, testable orchestration that covers BYOK import, mutual attestation, and a safe rotation plan. High level sequence below; I'll attach the network diagram and a draft runbook in a follow-up.

1) Prep & network: create a dedicated on-prem VPC segment for Redwood runtime, restrict egress to the HSM vendor's management IPs and Redwood control plane (if using private control plane). Ports: 443 for control plane, 5696/5697 for KMIP if using vendor HSM (optional), SSH for bastion access (jump host).

2) Provision HSM & split escrow: vendor provisions FIPS 140-2 Level 3 HSM. Generate unwrapped root key in HSM; produce split-escrow shares (2-of-3) stored with Acme security, vendor, and Redwood (when agreed).

3) BYOK import: Acme generates a customer key material export in a sealed, auditable token (signed by their KMS) and performs an online import into the HSM using vendor import token. Mutual attestation step: vendor signs device certificate, Redwood verifies certificate chain before accepting key import.

4) KEK wrapping: The HSM issues a tenant KEK, which wraps application data encryption keys (DEKs). DEKs are rotated on a scheduled window; KEK rotation is performed in HSM and rolled out via canary to a small percentage of requests.

5) Secrets handling: Redwood runtime keeps only wrapped DEKs in its KV cache. In-transit keys use TLS with mTLS for service-to-service calls. At rest, model parameters are encrypted with per-deployment DEKs stored only as wrapped blobs.

6) Rotation & rollback: Automated rotation pipeline (job in infra) performs new key generation inside HSM, rewraps DEKs, and updates runtime config. Rollback is supported by retaining previous KEK versions in HSM for 30 days and by a documented emergency unwrapping procedure requiring two custodians.

Questions for your infra team so I can finalize the runbook:
- Are we using the vendor's KMIP endpoint or vendor-specific import APIs?
- Do you want Redwood to hold one escrow share or should we operate without Redwood custody?
- Expected maintenance windows (preferred cadence/timezone)?

I'll follow up with the network diagram and a draft runbook (pdf) attached.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Sasha Patel <ops@acme-corp.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-11T08:30:00Z
Subject: Re: KMS/HSM plan for on-prem Private deployment (security questions)

Karthik / Sasha —

A few security-specific clarifications from my side before we land the runbook:

- Attestation: we require a vendor-signed attestation token that includes firmware versions and a device serial. Is the vendor comfortable providing signed audit logs for imports?
- Import policy: imports must be ephemeral (import key material stays in HSM and import tokens expire). We should deny any import that doesn't include a signed CSR from the HSM.
- Key usage separation: enforce that KEKs cannot be used for signing outside of wrapping/unwrapping (KMIP attribute controls).
- Audit retention: Acme needs 7 years of import/rotation audit events — confirm storage approach (push to Acme SIEM or vendor-hosted logs).

Also, on rotation: triggering rotation on-demand (security event) must be supported with a documented CRON fallback. We'll want an RBAC checklist for custodians who approve emergency rotations.

If vendor can confirm signed import logs and retention SLA, we can finalize sign-offs.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Security Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Marco Silva <hsm-vendor@crypto-hsm.io>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com, Sasha Patel <ops@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T16:10:00Z
Subject: Re: KMS/HSM plan for on-prem Private deployment (vendor details)

Hi all —

Thanks for including us. A few notes from the vendor side and attachments: I attached hsm_network_diagram_v2.png and vendor_byo_agreement.docx (redlined).

- We support KMIP and a vendor import API (we recommend KMIP + TLS mutual auth for most customers). Our management plane exposes a signed device cert and we can produce an import audit bundle (signed and timestamped) that includes firmware and serial.
- Split-escrow: we can produce M-of-N shares and provide hardware-backed secure export for the shares; Redwood holding one share is acceptable under a written escrow policy.
- Rotation: we provide an in-HSM key rotation primitive; bulk rewrap of DEKs is performed by the management client we ship. For performance-sensitive deployments, we recommend a rolling rewrap using a two-stage canary at 5% -> 25% -> 100%.

Security note: vendor export APIs produce an encrypted import token; we recommend the import token be delivered over an out-of-band channel (signed email + SFTP drop).

Happy to run a workshop with Acme infra and Redwood ops.

Regards,
Marco Silva
Head of Integration, Crypto HSM Inc.

Attachments: hsm_network_diagram_v2.png, vendor_byo_agreement.docx

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com, Sasha Patel <ops@acme-corp.com>, Marco Silva <hsm-vendor@crypto-hsm.io>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:00:00Z
Subject: Re: KMS/HSM plan for on-prem Private deployment (deployment sequence & canary)

Team —

I've converted Karthik's high-level sequence into an execution play for the first pilot (attached: kms_runbook_draft.pdf). Key operational items:

A) Preflight (Day 0-1)
  - Validate network ACLs: allow control-plane IPs, vendor management IPs; block all other outbound except fw updates.
  - Confirm HSM firmware and attestation certs; validate CRC/serial names against vendor bundle.

B) Import window (Day 2)
  - Bring HSM online behind vendor management VLAN. Perform mutual TLS handshake, pull signed device cert.
  - Use SFTP/out-of-band to receive encrypted import token. Perform import in maintenance window. Capture signed import audit bundle and push to Acme SIEM endpoint.

C) Canary rollout (Day 3-5)
  - Stage KEK into HSM, rewrap a 5% sample of DEKs in a separate canary namespace. Route 5% of inference traffic to runtime instances using new KEK. Monitor error rates, latency, and decrypt success.
  - If green, expand to 25% -> 100% in 2-day increments.

D) Post-deploy (Day 6)
  - Rotate short-term test keys and validate automated rollback procedure (two-custodian unseal). Ensure logs are archived to S3 with server-side encryption and the object keys are themselves wrapped by HSM KEK.

Operational cautions:
- Avoid mass rewrap during business hours; rewrap can spike IO and KV-store latency.
- Ensure KV cache eviction does not expose plaintext DEKs; all caches must only store wrapped blobs.

I recommend a 30-day observation window after the first full roll to tune rotation windows and canary thresholds.

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Product Ops, Redwood Inference

All —

This looks good. Procurement/legal reviewed the vendor_agreement redline and we have two open items before we can accept Redwood holding an escrow share: (1) explicit indemnity clause for escrow misuse; (2) audit rights to vendor logs for 24 months. Marco, can your team accept those as contract amendments?

Next steps for us to deliver to Acme:
- Finalize the network diagram and the runbook PDF (Vivek, Karthik: please attach the final versions to the INF-4321 ticket).
- Schedule a 90-min joint runbook walk-through with Acme and the vendor next week; Sasha, please propose availability.
- Confirm whether Redwood will take an escrow share or operate without it (Sasha + Acme security).

Once the contract points are closed we can plan a 2-week pilot start window.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Strategic Partnerships, Redwood Inference
